name: The Temporal Equivalence Principle: Suppressed Density Scaling in Globular Cluster Pulsars
description: Gravitational time dilation in General Relativity is confirmed to 10⁻⁵ precision in the Solar System. At intermediate astrophysical scales, however, persistent anomalies emerge. The Temporal Equivalence Principle (TEP) formalizes an alternative: that time dilation is scale-dependent. This work reports an 8.7σ dynamical anomaly in globular cluster pulsar timing that challenges standard density scaling (4.0σ tension). Analysis of 380 millisecond pulsars reveals a 0.13 dex excess in spin-down magnitude—cluster pulsars spin down faster than field controls. The signal exhibits Suppressed Density Scaling (Slope 0.35 vs Newtonian 0.82), saturating in dense cores. Complementary analysis of gravitational lensing provides geometric evidence for TEP at cosmological scales. DESJ0408 shows temporal shear of |Γ| ≈ 33 days/decade (2.2σ), geometrically consistent with saddle-point slowing. The combined analysis supports a coherent detection consistent with TEP screening in halo-scale potentials.
